original_question: In the one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z with infection density q > 0, suppose the initial distribution nu has exponentially decaying probability of containing no infected site in a symmetric interval around the origin, namely nu(no infected vertices in [-ell, ell]) = O(e^{-kappa ell}) for some kappa > 0. Under that assumption, is the convergence of the law at time t to the Bernoulli(q) equilibrium measure pi exponentially fast for every q > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 1.1, Conjecture 2 for the one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z, read together with Conjecture 1 / equation (1.1) for the exact meaning of convergence.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the target model (one-dimensional FA-1f on Z), the relevant stronger hypothesis on the initial law ν (an exponential tail for the event that a symmetric interval around 0 is completely healthy), the equilibrium measure π as Bernoulli(q), and the intended conclusion: exponential relaxation to equilibrium for all q. It is clearly aiming at the paper’s second conjecture in Section 1.1, not at a broader neighboring problem.
missing_details: The paper’s parameter range is q in (0,1), not merely q>0.
The state space should be made explicit: configurations η in {0,1}^Z, with 0 = infected and 1 = healthy.
The FA-1f dynamics should be identified explicitly: site x can update only if at least one nearest neighbor is infected; equivalently c_x(η)=1_{η_{x-1}=0 or η_{x+1}=0}.
The paper formulates convergence via local observables f (functions depending on finitely many vertices), not as an unspecified convergence of laws in infinite volume.
The baseline convergence statement being strengthened is equation (1.1): |E_ν[f(η(t))]-π(f)| -> 0 as t -> infinity for every local f.

The hypothesis should be stated in the paper’s interval language: the interval [-L,L] is healthy, i.e. contains no infected vertex; this means ν([-L,L] is healthy)=O(e^{-κL}) for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L.

The phrase 'exponentially fast' should be unpacked to a stand-alone bound, e.g. for every local f there exist C_f,c_f>0 such that |E_ν[f(η(t))]-π(f)| <= C_f e^{-c_f t} for all t>=0 (allowing dependence on f,q,ν).
The draft should identify π more explicitly as the Bernoulli product measure on {0,1}^Z with infected-site density q.
refined_question: For the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on Z, with state space {0,1}^Z, infected sites given by η_x=0, healthy sites by η_x=1, constraint c_x(η)=1_{η_{x-1}=0 or η_{x+1}=0}, and reversible Bernoulli product measure π=Ber(q)^{\otimes Z} with q in (0,1), suppose the initial law ν satisfies ν([-L,L] is healthy)=O(e^{-κL}) for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L. Is it true that, for every local function f depending on finitely many vertices, the convergence in equation (1.1), namely E_ν[f(η(t))] -> π(f) as t -> infinity, actually occurs at an exponential rate; equivalently, do there exist constants C_f,c_f>0 such that |E_ν[f(η(t))]-π(f)| <= C_f e^{-c_f t} for all t>=0?
justification: This is the paper’s second conjecture in Section 1.1. Your draft already matches its core content: FA-1f on Z, an exponential tail for the event that a large symmetric interval is entirely healthy, and exponential relaxation to the Bernoulli(q) equilibrium. The only substantive sharpening needed is to restore the paper’s exact convergence format from Conjecture 1 / equation (1.1): the statement is about all local observables f, not an unspecified topology on laws. Section 1.2 supplies the hidden notation ('infected', 'healthy', interval events, and π), and Section 1.4.1 supplies the FA-1f constraint. Because your draft is already narrowly pointed at this conjecture, it should not be broadened to later partial results or to other one-facilitated variants.
